# civgrad — sensitivity audit (the fog, measured)

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by `python3 -m analysis.sensitivity` — do not edit by hand. -->

Every capacity in the map and K_SAT are confidence-C session estimates.
The standing claim on every output is *trust the signs and rankings,*
*distrust the magnitudes*. This audit measures that claim: perturb the
confidence-C parameters (and, separately, the disruption prior), recompute
the gradients, and count what survives. Nothing here feeds back into the
frozen model or the scorecard.

**Protocol.** 500 seeded draws per sweep (PRNGKey(0)).
Parameter fog: each of the 13 transition capacities and K_SAT multiplied
by an independent lognormal factor, sigma=ln(2)/1.96 — 95% of factors
inside [x0.5, x2], the honest reading of confidence C. Prior fog:
scenario probabilities (lognormal, renormalized), severities
(logit-normal, sigma=0.5), and rebuild taus (lognormal) perturbed with
parameters frozen. A draw is *valid* when every gradient component is
finite (extreme draws can break the fixed-step integrator); stability is
reported over valid draws, with a worst-case floor counting every invalid
draw as a flipped sign.

## 1. Sign stability of the negative gradients

Each claim is audited only in the regime where the frozen baseline makes
it: the negative Pkg/Chips stockpile gradients exist in the
single-scenario run only (the prior-averaged baseline's stockpile
gradients are all positive).

| claim (baseline value, single / prior-avg) | single-scenario (param fog) | prior-averaged (param fog) | prior fog |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| d(thru)/d(cap) Ship_Strait < 0 (-2.68 / -1.63) | 89% (floor 89%) | 85% (floor 85%) | 100% |
| d(thru)/d(cap) Package < 0 (-1.70 / -0.37) | 51% (floor 51%) | 24% (floor 24%) | 84% |
| d(thru)/d(cap) Wear_EUV < 0 (-6.61 / -24.26) | 92% (floor 92%) | 91% (floor 91%) | 100% |
| d(thru)/d(stock) Pkg < 0 (-0.016 / —) | 21% (floor 21%) | — | — |
| d(thru)/d(stock) Chips < 0 (-0.020 / —) | 16% (floor 16%) | — | — |

Sign stability tracks magnitude, which is what it should do: the two
large negative gradients (shipping, wear) hold in ~85-92% of parameter-fog
draws and 100% of prior-fog draws; the near-zero negatives (Package
capacity, the Pkg/Chips stockpiles) flip freely — the model is confident
about the big signs and honestly noisy about the small ones. Claims built
on the small negatives do not survive audit and are not made anywhere in
the essay's headline results.

Valid draws: single 500/500, prior-averaged 500/500, prior fog 500/500.

## 2. Rankings under fog

| metric | single-scenario | prior-averaged | prior fog |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| top capacity in the production/equipment complex | 99% | 91% | 100% |
| top stockpile an equipment or fab-input stock | 100% | 90% | 100% |
| modal #1 capacity | Build_EUV (36%) | Build_EUV (23%) | Fab (94%) |
| Fab ranked #1 capacity | 9% | 10% | 94% |
| exact top-3 capacity set unchanged | 2% | 6% | 55% |
| Kendall tau vs baseline ranking (mean) | 0.53 | 0.47 | 0.92 |
| Kendall tau (10th percentile) | 0.31 | 0.13 | 0.85 |
| boneyard: worn > working spares | 20% | 12% | 0% |

Reading: **what survives parameter fog is the partition, not the
ordering.** In ~99%/91% of draws the top capacity sits in the
production/equipment complex — the downstream logistics chain leads
essentially never — and the top stockpile is an equipment or fab-input
stock, not downstream inventory. But WHICH node inside the complex leads
is fog-conditional (Fab is #1 in only ~10% of parameter-fog draws;
Build_EUV is the modal leader), full rank order runs Kendall tau ~0.5,
and the boneyard-on-top ordering survives only in a minority of draws —
the honest version of that result is *comparable value*, not *highest
value*. Under prior fog alone (parameters held at their estimates) the
full ranking is stable (tau ~0.9, Fab #1 in ~94%): the ranking's
weakness is parameter ignorance, not prior choice — which is exactly
what data PRs with real citations would sharpen.

## 3. Is the Sumitomo miss structural?

Re-running the Sumitomo 1993 v1 replay under the same parameter fog:
**95% of 500 draws still miss the
frozen acceptance band** (dip 15±15%, recovery 3±3 mo);
45% never recover within the 72-month
horizon (median dip 96%). The miss is not a
bad-parameter accident a data PR could fix — it is structural, which is
exactly what the missing-mechanism diagnosis (no price-mediated
allocation; PLAN.md §5, PRICE_EXPERIMENT.md) predicts.

**Caveats.** The fog model is itself a modeling choice (independent
lognormal factors; no correlated errors). The disruption prior has five
scenarios — prior fog explores their neighborhood, not scenarios the
prior cannot express. And the pessimism-bias caveat travels with every
number here: no price-mediated allocation, so depths and durations are
overstated (SCORECARD.md).
